references.text: Continuation of the account of the five kings who hid in a cave at Makkedah
The five kings are brought out of the cave, executed and hung on trees, then placed back in the cave
Identifies the five kings who fled: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon
Background to the coalition of kings that fought against Israel
Similar pattern where hostile kings hide in caves from the Israelites
David hides in a cave at Adullam, showing caves as places of refuge in the same geographic area
Saul enters a cave where David is hiding, another example of caves as hiding places
Psalm written when David was in a cave, thematically connected to hiding in caves
Prophecy that people will hide in caves and mountain clefts from the Lord's wrath
The kings of the earth and the mighty hide in caves and mountains on the day of judgment, a similar motif of fleeing kings
